prompt: Which list contains only main features of a MANET shown in the lesson?
options: Self-forming and self-healing, fixed number of members, frequency hopping, unicast, multicast and broadcast support, quality of service
Self-forming and self-healing, dynamic number of members, centralized administration, unicast, multicast and broadcast support, quality of service
Self-forming and self-healing, dynamic number of members, frequency hopping, unicast, multicast and broadcast support, quality of service
Self-forming and self-healing, dynamic number of members, frequency hopping, permanent wired backbone, quality of service
explanation: Page 12 shows these five main features of a MANET. References: MANET C4ISTAR Planning, page 12.

prompt: Which pairing of waveform and description is correct?
options: STANAG 4204: encrypted analog and digital voice; CNR: non-encrypted analog voice
STANAG 4204: non-encrypted analog voice; CNR: encrypted analog and digital voice
STANAG 4204: compatible with Elbit legacy systems; CNR: compatible with the NATO waveform
WMA-HC: non-encrypted analog voice; CNR: compatible with the NATO waveform
explanation: Pages 35 and 36 give STANAG 4204 as non-encrypted analog voice and CNR as encrypted analog and digital voice. References: MANET C4ISTAR Planning, pages 35, 36.

prompt: Which pairing of maintenance type and activity is correct?
options: Preventive maintenance: visual inspection and cleaning; fault procedure: identification, isolation, repair, verification
Preventive maintenance: fault isolation and repair; fault procedure: visual inspection and cleaning of the equipment
Preventive maintenance: fault verification; fault procedure: cleaning of the panel and controls only
Preventive maintenance: fault identification and repair; fault procedure: visual inspection of the cables only
explanation: Pages 24 to 26 describe preventive maintenance as visual inspection and cleaning; page 27 gives the four-step fault procedure. References: MANET C4ISTAR Planning, pages 24, 25, 26, 27.

prompt: Which pairing of operational mode and use is correct?
options: OTP: return to normal operation; MTP: maintenance mode for recovering from a technical fault
OTP: normal mode with many programming cycles; MTP: one-time maintenance after a fault
OTP: loading of software updates; MTP: loading of operational parameters at the operator level
OTP: maintenance mode for recovering from a technical fault; MTP: return to normal operation
explanation: Page 68 describes OTP as the maintenance mode for recovering from a technical fault and MTP as the return to normal operation. References: MANET C4ISTAR Planning, page 68.

prompt: Which two Integrator best practices address unneeded traffic and traffic crossing into other networks, in that order?
options: Deny traffic leaking; reduce traffic
Security; reduce traffic
Dynamic routing; deny traffic leaking
Reduce traffic; deny traffic leaking
explanation: Page 70 lists reduce traffic and deny traffic leaking among the best practices of the Integrator. References: MANET C4ISTAR Planning, page 70.

prompt: Bulk reports and urgent updates share one limited link, and operators cannot process everything. Which pairing names the two problems?
options: Quality of service for the link; data overload for the operators
Data overload for the link; quality of service for the operators
Self-healing for the link; feedback for the operators
Frequency hopping for the link; data overload for the operators
explanation: QoS addresses competing traffic on limited network resources, while data overload is more information than operators can process; feedback informs decision-makers as conditions change. References: MANET C4ISTAR Planning, page 9; C4ISTAR Sensors Integration, page 18; C4ISTAR Weapon System Integration, slide 14.

prompt: A design uses frequency hopping and a redundant radio. Which statement matches each measure with what the lessons say it does?
options: Frequency hopping keeps one failure from compromising the system; redundancy protects the transmission
Frequency hopping protects the management exchange; redundancy protects the transmission
Frequency hopping adds capabilities to the system; redundancy allows components to be upgraded
Frequency hopping protects the transmission; redundancy keeps one failure from compromising the system
explanation: Frequency hopping contributes to transmission protection, and redundancy prevents one failure from compromising the entire system; neither establishes confidentiality, integrity and availability by itself. References: MANET C4ISTAR Planning, page 30; C4ISTAR Weapon System Integration, slide 24; C4ISTAR Sensors Integration, page 29.

prompt: A faulty radio has been isolated and repaired. Which step of the troubleshooting model comes next, and what shows that it worked?
options: Fault identification, shown by the radio's indicator lights
Fault isolation, shown by the repair record
Repair verification, shown by tests and observed service results
Repair verification, shown by a visual inspection alone
explanation: Fault repair is followed by repair verification (including BIT); verification tests and observed service results give the evidence, and sensor integration adds that information must reach its users. References: MANET C4ISTAR Planning, page 27; C4ISTAR Sensors Integration, page 9.

prompt: In the node information, RSSI is high but SNR is low near electrical equipment. What do the two values measure?
options: RSSI is received signal quality relative to noise; SNR is received signal strength
RSSI is received signal strength; SNR is received signal quality relative to noise
RSSI is the distance to the remote node; SNR is the data rate received
RSSI is the number of packets received; SNR is the number of packets sent
explanation: RSSI is received signal strength and SNR measures the received signal quality between the remote and local nodes; electromagnetic interference affects sensor performance and the feedback loop depends on actual delivery. References: MANET C4ISTAR Planning, page 56; C4ISTAR Sensors Integration, page 18; C4ISTAR Weapon System Integration, slide 14.

prompt: A gateway passes a TCP/IP data test, but voice fails. Which statement is correct?
options: The voice requirement is met because TCP/IP is a common standard
Meeting the ICD ends the need to test voice
The data result is invalid because voice and data must succeed together
The data result stands on its own; voice needs separate integration and verification
explanation: Voice integration is distinguished from data integration; TCP/IP gives a standard framework and the ICD defines the exchange, but neither shows that voice works. References: MANET C4ISTAR Planning, pages 72, 73; C4ISTAR Sensors Integration, page 16; C4ISTAR Weapon System Integration, slide 23.

prompt: Which of the following is NOT a benefit the lesson attributes to integrated sensor data in the COP?
options: Accurate counterfire against enemy firing positions
Efficient logistics
Collaborative planning
Spectrum licensing for civilian broadcasters
explanation: Page 9 lists situational awareness, focused intelligence, collaborative planning, mobility and flexibility, efficient logistics and accurate counterfire. References: C4ISTAR Sensors Integration, page 9.

prompt: A UAS and an SUGV are both listed as mobile or remote platforms. What do they do for fixed sensors?
options: Replace fixed sensors in the loop and the decision-maker
Carry other sensors to where fixed ones can't reach
Relay sensor data to GHQ over BONTEX
Provide the decision-maker's analysis
explanation: Page 15: UAS and SUGV carry other sensors to where fixed ones cannot reach. References: C4ISTAR Sensors Integration, page 15.

prompt: Which pairing of term and definition is correct?
options: NISP: describes a system's interfaces and communication rules
IOP: prescribes technical standards across an alliance
ICD: describes a system's interfaces and communication rules
Open architecture: defines the connection points between national networks
explanation: Page 16: the ICD describes interfaces and communication rules; NISP prescribes alliance standards; IOP are connection points; open architecture allows add-ons. References: C4ISTAR Sensors Integration, page 16.

prompt: Which pairing of constraint and meaning is correct?
options: Cost: developing, deploying, and maintaining sensor capability is expensive and must fit budget constraints
Data overload: older systems may not be compatible with new sensors and backward compatibility must be engineered in
Legacy integration: ISR sources generate more data than operators can process
Human factors: urban, desert and mountainous terrain affect reliability
explanation: Page 18 lists cost as the expense of developing, deploying and maintaining sensor capability within budget constraints. References: C4ISTAR Sensors Integration, page 18.

prompt: Which statement about the ASR and the AIR is correct?
options: AIR installs, repairs and maintains all C4 hardware and software in coordination with ASR
ASR installs, repairs and maintains C4ISTAR hardware and software in coordination with AIR
ASR owns the ISTAR sensors while AIR owns the core C4 systems
ASR and AIR share end-user preventive maintenance
explanation: Page 27: ASR handles installation, repair and maintenance of C4ISTAR hardware and software in coordination with AIR, which owns the ISTAR core systems. References: C4ISTAR Sensors Integration, page 27.

prompt: Which list shows what integrated sensor data feeds into the Common Operational Picture?
options: Situational awareness, focused intelligence, collaborative planning, mobility, efficient logistics and accurate counterfire
Situational awareness, focused intelligence, legal review, mobility, efficient logistics and accurate counterfire
Situational awareness, focused intelligence, collaborative planning, mobility, personnel replacement and accurate counterfire
Situational awareness, force structure, collaborative planning, mobility, efficient logistics and accurate counterfire
explanation: Integrated sensor data feeds the COP: battlespace situational awareness, focused intelligence, collaborative planning, mobility and flexibility, efficient logistics and accurate counterfire; more reports alone do not guarantee understanding. References: C4ISTAR Sensors Integration, pages 9, 18; C4ISTAR Weapon System Integration, slide 8.

prompt: How many radio direction finding measurements are needed to locate an unknown transmitter, and what does a single one give?
options: One measurement; it gives the exact position
Two or more measurements; each gives an exact position
Two or more measurements; a single one gives a direction toward the source
Three or more measurements; a single one gives the transmitter's identity
explanation: Ground-based RDF finds the direction of a radio source and two or more measurements locate the transmitter; intelligence then interprets the information. References: C4ISTAR Sensors Integration, pages 9, 10; C4ISTAR Weapon System Integration, slide 8.

prompt: A component is upgraded under modular design. What does modular design preserve, and which document says how its messages are exchanged?
options: Compatibility; the Interface Control Document
Redundancy; the Interface Control Document
Compatibility; the NATO Interoperability Standards and Profiles
Open architecture; the Service Interoperability Point
explanation: Modular design allows components to be replaced or upgraded while preserving compatibility, and the ICD describes the interfaces and information-exchange rules; interoperability also includes people and processes. References: C4ISTAR Sensors Integration, pages 16, 29; C4ISTAR Weapon System Integration, slide 18.

prompt: Which design requirement protects a sensor against electronic warfare and EMP?
options: EMI and radio-frequency shielding
Redundancy of components
Modular design
Regular operational and acceptance testing
explanation: EMI and radio-frequency shielding protects the sensor against electronic warfare and other electromagnetic threats; redundancy prevents one failure from compromising the system, and verification tests give evidence of performance. References: C4ISTAR Sensors Integration, pages 18, 29; MANET C4ISTAR Planning, page 27.

prompt: A fault crosses the boundary between core C4 systems and ISTAR sensors. Which pairing assigns installation, operation and maintenance correctly?
options: AIR for the core C4 systems; ASR for the ISTAR core systems
ASR for both the core C4 and ISTAR systems
ASR for the core C4 systems; AIR for the ISTAR core systems
The using unit for core C4 systems; AIR for ISTAR core systems
explanation: The Army Signal Regiment handles the core C4 systems and the Army Intelligence Regiment the ISTAR core systems; both are actors in the PA C4ISTAR architectural framework. References: C4ISTAR Sensors Integration, page 27; C4ISTAR Weapon System Integration, slide 29.

prompt: A unit watches a river approach, a satellite pass and a network segment continuously, using visual, electronic and aural means, to keep situational awareness. Which C4ISTAR component is this?
options: Surveillance
Reconnaissance
Intelligence
Target Acquisition
explanation: Systematic observation of areas, persons, activities, objects or domains, including aerospace and cyberspace, is surveillance. References: C4ISTAR Weapon System Integration, slide 11.

prompt: A commander directs forces and employs resources, while supporting systems collect, process, display, store and disseminate information. Which pair does this describe?
options: Surveillance and reconnaissance
Command and control
Communications and computers
Intelligence and target acquisition
explanation: Command is the authority to direct forces and employ resources; control is the activities and systems that handle the information. References: C4ISTAR Weapon System Integration, slide 7.

prompt: A unit's legacy radios, cellular, Wi-Fi and IPVPN links must all keep its COP current. Which interoperability principle does this rely on?
options: Seamless interconnectivity through multiple media
Open architecture of the PA C4ISTAR framework
Standardized networking and data exchange over TCP/IP
Interoperability through defined Interoperability Points
explanation: The Army operates an amalgam of media, and seamless communications let troops and commanders keep SA and COP. References: C4ISTAR Weapon System Integration, slide 21.

prompt: A planner claims that open architecture and TCP/IP alone ensure that only authorized users get access. Which lesson statement answers this?
options: Open architecture replaces authorization with common standards for every user and device
Interoperability is not unrestricted connectivity; authentication and access controls still apply
TCP/IP provides encryption and access control by default for all connected systems
Security measures apply only to legacy systems that lack open interfaces
explanation: The lesson says interoperability does not mean unrestricted connectivity and names authentication, authorization and access controls among the measures. References: C4ISTAR Weapon System Integration, slides 22, 24.

prompt: A design is reviewed only against documented equipment specifications, interfaces and applicable standards. Which limitation applies?
options: Interoperability with the specified standards cannot be determined from the documented elements
Performance against the documented equipment limits cannot be assessed from the same elements
Compatibility between the proposed interfaces cannot be assessed from the documented elements
Its suitability for the intended environment and users cannot be established from those elements alone
explanation: Specifications, interfaces and standards show what the design contains, not how suitable it is for its environment and users; the lesson treats these as conceptual roles and relationships. References: C4ISTAR Weapon System Integration, slides 26, 29.

prompt: Which statement describes 'control' as distinct from 'command' in the C2 system?
options: It is the commander's authority and responsibility to direct forces
It provides the reliable links for issuing orders and receiving feedback
It includes the activities and systems used to collect, process, display, store and disseminate information
It detects, locates and identifies a target for weapons employment
explanation: Command is the authority and responsibility to direct forces and employ resources, while control includes the activities and systems used to collect, process, display, store and disseminate relevant information; integration connects that information to users. References: C4ISTAR Weapon System Integration, slides 7, 11; C4ISTAR Sensors Integration, page 9.

prompt: Two systems pass a format test through an integrator, yet their teams apply different reporting procedures. Which statement describes the situation?
options: Interoperability is complete because the ICD was met
The integrator failed to connect the two systems
Only the equipment needs to be replaced
Technical exchange works, but procedural interoperability is incomplete
explanation: Interoperability covers people, processes, technology and information systems; the ICD defines technical interfaces and the integrator connects the services, but procedures must be harmonized. References: C4ISTAR Weapon System Integration, slide 18; C4ISTAR Sensors Integration, page 16; MANET C4ISTAR Planning, page 71.

prompt: A proposal forwards every report to all connected accounts for easy access. Which lesson points does it contradict?
options: Using open architecture and multiple communication media
Defining Interoperability Points and common standards
Limiting unnecessary traffic and the rule that interoperability is not unrestricted connectivity
Using frequency hopping and embedded TRANSEC
explanation: Security must accompany interoperability, and the MANET lesson's best practices are to deny traffic leaking and reduce traffic; confidentiality, integrity and availability still need protection. References: C4ISTAR Weapon System Integration, slide 24; MANET C4ISTAR Planning, page 70.

prompt: A TCP/IP test delivers packets, but the receiving application reads one status value wrongly. Which document defines how the receiving system should interpret the data?
options: The TCP/IP framework
The Interface Control Document
The Interoperability Point protocol stack
The D3A process
explanation: The ICD describes the interface and information-exchange rules, including how the receiving system interprets the information; TCP/IP only provides the standardized network framework. References: C4ISTAR Weapon System Integration, slides 16, 21, 23; C4ISTAR Sensors Integration, page 16.

prompt: In the sensor, decision-maker and shooter loop, which role provides information back to decision-makers as the operational environment changes?
options: The sensor
The shooter
The decision-maker
The integrator
explanation: Shooters execute the plans while also providing information back to decision-makers as conditions change; verification tests and observed results show whether the service delivers it. References: C4ISTAR Weapon System Integration, slides 14, 29; MANET C4ISTAR Planning, page 27.
